record.original_question: Given a finite lattice K, find a test that decides whether K is isomorphic to the congruence lattice Con(N) of some antilattice N.

evidence.quote: Given a finite lattice K. Find a test that will tell whether K is isomorphic to a congruence lattice Con(N ) of some antilattice.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An antilattice is an algebra $(N;\vee,\wedge)$ of type $(2,2)$ satisfying the same axioms as a lattice except that the commutativity laws for $\vee$ and $\wedge$ are replaced by their anticommutative analogues: for all $x,y\in N$, if $x\vee y=y\vee x$ then $x=y$, and if $x\wedge y=y\wedge x$ then $x=y$ (equivalently, both operations are anticommutative idempotent operations satisfying associativity and the absorption laws). A congruence on $N$ is an equivalence relation compatible with both $\vee$ and $\wedge$, and $\mathrm{Con}(N)$ denotes the lattice of all congruences of $N$ under inclusion.

Problem. Provide an effective decision procedure (a test) that, given an arbitrary finite lattice $K$ as input, determines whether there exists an antilattice $N$ such that $\mathrm{Con}(N)$ is isomorphic to $K$. Equivalently, characterize the class of finite lattices that arise (up to isomorphism) as congruence lattices of antilattices.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem of characterizing which finite lattices arise as congruence lattices of antilattices appears to remain open. Related work on regular antilattices and elementary/odd/simple/irreducible antilattices (Cvetko-Vah, Kinyon, Leech, Pisanski, and others) studies congruences of antilattices but does not provide a general recognition test for finite congruence lattices of antilattices. No source found announcing a solution.

status_evidence.title: Regular Antilattices
status_evidence.snippet: Antilattices for which Green's equivalences are congruences are studied; congruence structure of antilattices is investigated but no general recognition theorem is given.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work studies congruences of antilattices in special subclasses, but does not provide a decision test for arbitrary finite lattices to be congruence lattices of antilattices.

status_evidence.title: On elementary, odd, semimagic and other classes of antilattices
status_evidence.snippet: Studies simple antilattices (no nontrivial congruences) and other classes, indicating the structural study of congruences of antilattices is ongoing.
status_evidence.claim: The classification of congruence lattices of antilattices is still under active investigation.
